title: Graph Decompositions at the Integral Expectation Threshold

issues.description: The whole large-degeneracy case depends on the companion's same-parameter discrete-convexity theorem (OpenAI26DC Thm 1.1, i.e. Talagrand Conj. 7.1 with K0=2^75 and the cover at the same r). This paper does not prove it and this audit did not verify it. This is a disclosed dependency, not a gap. Even if the companion only held at parameter r/L, the argument would still work with r = L'q and a constant loss.
issues.evidence: Corollary 2.2 proof: F_H ⊆ E_{K0}(D) and then Theorem 2.1 supplies a cost ≤1/2 cover at r>q. Nothing else in the paper supplies this.

coverage: I read the whole paper (sections 1–4). Checked line by line: Corollary 2.2; Lemma 2.3 (both lower bounds on q); degeneracy splitting; the compression lemma (each increment > r^s/2, at most ⌈2r^{-s}⌉ additions, conditional-law argument); the neighborhood transfer proposition (source mean x via τ=1-(1-r)^2; independence; Hoeffding bound exp(-cn^{0.98}) against log #tests ≲ n^{2/3}log n + n^{1/100}log^2 n; the amplification x* ≥ 1-(1-x)^16; both Hall regimes, numerically verified (1-e^{-1})·16 ≥ 8 and 0.237n > n/8); the max-degree embedding (layer construction with ≤4s earlier neighbors, t=O(s log n), bin sizes, fresh exposures, conflict graph degree ≤4sΔ, exponent 1-2/3-4/100=22/75, union bound n^{2u}); the star-forest proposition (cover-count bound (2.x), Paley–Zygmund ≥1/6, small-mean bound giving 100^ℓ m_ℓ/(2en), E T ≤ (3/100+2e/99)n < n/8, Markov); the assembly (Y0 size ≤2d√n, closure argument giving |Y| ≤ 2|Y0|, d<2log n/log2, s ≤ 3d/M when d≥M, r^s ≥ n^{-6/M}, applicability of each proposition to each piece type, piece counts ≤ k, small-n and q ≥ 1/(2A) trivial cases, the bounded-degeneracy parity star-forest split, monotonicity of q).
main_claim: There are absolute constants k and L such that for every graph H on at most n vertices, E(H) can be partitioned into k pieces H_i (fixed before sampling) with p_c(H_i;n) ≤ L·q(H;n), where q is the integral expectation threshold. This resolves AHPT Conjecture 8.1.
sibling_notes: Family 175 board was empty. I found no sibling audit of the discrete-convexity companion (OpenAI26DC) anywhere on the hive. That companion is the sole external dependency.
